text:
riley: Heads-up: new customer hit a crash only on production builds (webpack+terser) when using our JS SDK on an edge deploy. Dev server + node OK.

karen: ouch, what exactly crashed? stack? repro?

riley: Error: `ReferenceError: Request is not defined` from inside our auth/retry wrapper on first outbound call. Happens after `npm run build:prod && serve -s dist` (simulating edge bundle).

riley: Repro steps (minimal):
```bash
# clone minimal repro
git clone git@github.com:internal/sample-repros/redwood-edge-webpack-repro.git
cd redwood-edge-webpack-repro
npm ci
# build prod (webpack + terser)
npm run build:prod
# serve static files
npx serve dist -l 5000
# hit POST /api/complete
curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/api/complete -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
```

riley: The bundle contains a small helper `attachFetchGlobals()` that we expect to run in edge contexts if `Request`/`Headers` are missing. In prod build, terser/webpack inlines `typeof Request !== 'undefined'` as true and removes the helper completely because our guard was in a branch that terser deems dead.

karen: so tree-shaking + minifier constant-folding removed the polyfill. Which entrypoint did webpack pick? module or main? Also do you have sideEffects: false in package.json?

riley: Webpack picked the ESM `module` field (index.mjs). The SDK package has `sideEffects: false` at the root (we added that ages ago). The helper lived in the same module and was only referenced inside a conditional; with sideEffects false and no top-level import it got dropped.

tony: iirc rollup behaves differently; earlier we saw Vite's optimizeDeps would keep it. Can we trigger consistently in rollup/webpack?

riley: repro shows webpack+terser fails, rollup build (esbuild minify) preserved it, Vite dev preserved. So it's minifier/optimizer specific.

karen: workaround for users?

riley: temporary workarounds we suggested to customer: 1) import side-effectful shim explicitly in server entry `import 'redwood/edge-policy'` 2) set `sideEffects: true` in SDK package (but that has perf/regressions for other apps) 3) add a tiny explicit call `import { ensureEdgeGlobals } from 'redwood'; ensureEdgeGlobals();` in their app. We prefer (1) or (3) until we ship a proper fix.

tony: for a proper SDK fix we should: - move the guard into its own entry file that's always referenced from the published `exports` map - avoid branching on `typeof Request` at build-time (use runtime check that can't be const-folded) - add a small comment so terser doesn't fold it? maybe use `/*#__PURE__*/` tricks?

riley: i tried a tiny change: replace `if (typeof Request === 'undefined')` with `if (globalThis.Request === undefined)` and that prevented terser folding in my local experiment (because globalThis is non-const for the minifier config). But that's fragile.

karen: also types issue: the ESM `index.mjs` ships `.d.ts` from `types/esm/index.d.ts` but our published types bundle lacked the extended `retry` union for the new options. Customer's TS build showed `Property 'retries' does not exist on type`.

riley: repro for TS: in a fresh TS app `client.generate({ prompt: 'x', retry: { retries: 2 } })` => tsc error. Workaround: `import type { ClientOptions } from 'redwood/dist/types';` then cast. Not acceptable for onboarding.

tony: action items:
- SDK: split edge-shim into its own file and reference it from the ESM entrypoint (tony)
- Publish: ensure `types` for ESM contain retry options (karen + release)
- Devex: add quickstart note with Vite/webpack caveats + sample `ensureEdgeGlobals()` snippet (docs-onboard)
- CI: add a smoke build for webpack/rollup/vite prod builds that runs a local static server + curl check (build-bot)

build-bot: created job RED-3301 to add bundler smoke tests to CI (https://internal/ci/RED-3301) :gear:

riley: here's minimal code we used to repro the failing SDK bundle (pasted from built `dist/vendor/redwood.js`):
```js
// merged bundle snippet (after terser)
var maybeAttach = function(){if(typeof Request!=='undefined'){return}else{globalThis.Headers = globalThis.Headers || function(){/* poly */}}};
// later unused
```

riley: notice how terser replaces the full runtime check and keeps a no-op because it thinks Request exists. The actual call site was behind `if (opts.retry)` so the whole export was removed.

karen: OK I'll flag `edge-bundler-interop` and `types-esm` on the issue. Tony, can you prototype the export-split and add an SDK unit test that simulates webpack minify?

tony: yes. I can add a small rollup/webpack build in the SDK repo under `tests/bundler-repro/*` and add it to release CI as a separate job. I'll also include a small README for contributors.

docs-onboard: I'll add a short FAQ entry to the quickstart: "If you see missing Request/Headers at runtime after a production bundle, add an explicit SDK shim import or include the SDK in optimizeDeps for Vite/ESBuild. Example: `import { ensureEdgeGlobals } from 'redwood'; ensureEdgeGlobals();`"

riley: filing the minimal repro repo under internal and linking to RED-3301. Will open a PR to quickstart with the snippet today.

karen: thanks all. we should also add a short note in the SDK changelog when fixed so customers can upgrade safely.

riley: agreed — will comment on the issue when a release with the fix is cut.
